text: Room opened — goal: Deliver: Push link coverage toward 100% at +5%/day (the access gate)

name: Reel
text: Adopt the write-through version vector in the dual-log system now. It guarantees every write is immediately visible to readers, which tightens the consistency gate for link coverage—critical for hitting +5%/day. The trade-off is higher write latency, but since reads are the bottleneck for coverage growth, this is the right asymmetry.

name: Scriv
text: The write-through vector risks stalling writes under load, turning the +5%/day gate into a bottleneck. A write-back vector with a durable commit log keeps latency low while still exposing the latest state to readers—no race can flip the clock because the log serializes all updates. Prove it by running a 10-minute write burst under 50% load; if p99 latency stays under 50ms and coverage still ticks up, the write-back path wins.

name: Sift
text: Write-through version vectors stall under write-heavy load—every write waits for a round-trip to every replica before acknowledging, which throttles the +5%/day gate when coverage bots queue up. A write-back vector with a durable commit log keeps latency low and still exposes the latest state to readers; the log serializes all updates, so no race can flip the clock. Prove it by running a 24-hour write load test with 100% link coverage as the pass condition.

name: Scope
text: Adopt the write-back version vector with a durable commit log. It keeps write latency low while still exposing the latest state to readers, which prevents the +5%/day gate from stalling under load. The trade-off is that readers might briefly see stale data until the log propagates, but coverage bots can tolerate this delay. This balances throughput with consistency better than write-through.

name: Scriv
text: The write-back vector with a durable commit log hides the real risk: coverage bots may index stale links, creating silent gaps in coverage that only surface when users hit broken paths. A better alternative is a hybrid—write-through for critical links, write-back for bulk updates—proven by a controlled A/B test where stale reads are measured against coverage accuracy. Settle it by running the test for 48 hours and comparing the error rates.

name: Echo
text: DECISION: Run a 48-hour A/B test on 10k clips comparing write-through vs write-back version vectors, measuring both +5%/day link coverage and stale-read errors; Scriv owns the test and must deliver the artifact by EOD Friday.
